usage_boundary: For management diagnosis and discussion. These distinctions are not industry definitions, external benchmarks, client outcomes or disclosures of any company's internal system.

comparisons.direct_answer: An SOP defines how a task should be performed. An operating system connects standards to responsibility, training, field execution, inspection, correction, verification and controlled updates.

left.name: SOP
left.proves: A task method has been documented
left.does_not_prove: People can execute it consistently across roles and stores

right.name: Operating system
right.proves: The organization has connected mechanisms for repeatable execution and learning

comparisons.decision_rule: Use an SOP for task clarity; build the wider operating system when consistent multi-person or multi-store execution matters.

comparisons.direct_answer: Training completion proves participation in a learning activity. Capability certification requires observed performance against defined criteria under relevant operating conditions.

left.name: Training completion
left.proves: The learner attended, viewed or finished assigned content
left.does_not_prove: The learner can perform independently and reliably

comparisons.decision_rule: Use completion for exposure and compliance tracking; require certification before assigning critical independent work.

comparisons.direct_answer: Inspection identifies and records a deviation. Closed-loop governance carries the issue through ownership, correction, evidence, verification, closure, recurrence analysis and prevention.

left.name: Inspection
left.proves: A condition was checked and a deviation may have been identified
left.does_not_prove: The cause was corrected or recurrence was prevented

right.name: Closed-loop governance
right.proves: The issue moved through accountable correction and verified closure

comparisons.decision_rule: Use inspection to detect; use closed-loop governance whenever the deviation is material, recurring or risk-bearing.
